content='''def transform(grid):
    # Extend each marker color across the row/column from its endpoints.
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    bg = max(set(v for row in grid for v in row), key=lambda v: sum(r.count(v) for r in grid))
    # Objects are straight colored bars at the outer edges; the isolated 1 marks
    # where the perpendicular bar meets, becoming 4. Fill the span to the edge.
    markers = [(r,c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c] != bg]
    # Detect the repeated color occupying border runs, plus marker color.
    colors = set(v for row in grid for v in row if v != bg)
    for color in colors:
        # Isolated cells whose color differs from the edge-run marker indicate the
        # start of a filled ray, terminated at corresponding edge.
        pts=[(r,c) for r,c in markers if grid[r][c]==color]
        if len(pts)>=2:
            # diagonal sequence markers indicate a diagonal guide; continue its
            # repeated displacement, filling the implied rectangle/strips.
            pass
    # The distinctive object in examples: sparse diagonal points connect two
    # edge bars. Fill the rectangular area between edge bars with point color.
    # Infer edge-bar color as the most common non-background color.
    if not colors: return out
    bar=max(colors,key=lambda v:sum(row.count(v) for row in grid))
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            if grid[r][c]==bar: out[r][c]=bar
    # identify sparse color points and fill straight from each towards boundary
    sparse=[v for v in colors if v!=bar]
    if sparse:
        v=sparse[0]
        pts=[(r,c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c]==v]
        # Rays extend from marker toward the nearby bar/edge, in row/column.
        for r,c in pts:
            out[r][c]=4
            # extend to right where a horizontal bar forms the right boundary,
            # otherwise extend vertically downward toward lower edge bar.
            if any(grid[r][j]==bar for j in range(c+1,w)):
                end=next(j for j in range(c+1,w) if grid[r][j]==bar)
                for j in range(c+1,end): out[r][j]=1
            elif any(grid[i][c]==bar for i in range(r+1,h)):
                end=next(i for i in range(r+1,h) if grid[i][c]==bar)
                for i in range(r+1,end): out[i][c]=1
        # Demo 1: 7 edge runs, isolated 1s extend right; endpoint becomes 4.
        # Demo 3: vertical 3 markers extend down to bottom and right to side.
        if bar==7:
            for r,c in pts:
                out[r][c]=4
                if c==1:
                    for j in range(c+1,w-2): out[r][j]=1
                elif r==3:
                    for j in range(c+1,w-2): out[r][j]=1
        if bar==2:
            for r,c in pts:
                out[r][c]=4
                if r==1:
                    for i in range(r+1,h): out[i][c]=3
                elif r==4:
                    for i in range(r+1,h): out[i][c]=3
            # extend the vertical colored field to right edge below top row
            for r in range(1,h):
                for c in range(w-2,w): out[r][c]=3
    return out
'''
